title: Loubieh B'Joz (Green Beans with Walnuts and Garlic)
steps: Boil the green beans for 5 minutes, checking often so they stay crisp and bright green.
Drain and plunge them straight into ice water to stop the cooking. Drain well.

Make the sauce: pulse the walnuts, pine nuts, garlic, and a little of the olive oil into a thick, coarse paste. With an immersion blender, use a tall narrow container and short bursts, scraping down between them. Stop while it still has texture; if it starts going smooth, finish by hand.
Toss the green beans with the walnut mixture until everything is well coated.
notes: Optional: serve the beans on a bed of labneh with a little lemon zest over the top. Labneh makes it no longer vegan or dairy-free. Keep the sauce coarse: an immersion blender or food processor in short bursts works, but a high-speed blender runs straight past coarse into walnut butter. Make up any pine nuts left out with more walnuts.
freezeNote: The walnut-garlic sauce freezes well on its own; blanched green beans come back limp. Make a double batch of sauce, freeze half, cook beans fresh each time.
